title: Unified Inference: Q3 2026 Product Overview, PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap & Pricing
author: Sofia Martinez
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the Q3 2026 product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design specs, roadmap themes, pricing and packaging notes, and release/rollout plan for the Unified Inference product family (hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, and Redwood Private). It is intended for product, engineering, sales, and customer success stakeholders.

Goals (Q3 2026)

- Deliver a single, consistent developer experience for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Reduce median per-token cost for typical web-chat workloads by 20% through batching, caching, and quantization recommendations.
- Improve reliability: achieve 99.95% availability for hosted API and <1% error rate for p50 request success.
- Launch the new Pricing & Packaging model v2 with clearer dedicated capacity tiers and an opt-in usage discount for qualifying customers.

Problem Statement

Customers building LLM features need predictable latency, transparent unit economics, and a single API/UX across deployment modes. Today: multiple model variants, inconsistent rollout policies, and fragmented pricing create operational friction for engineering teams and procurement.

Success Metrics

- Platform availability: 99.95% (monthly) for hosted API endpoints.
- Latency: p95 generation latency < 300ms for short-turn tasks (<128 tokens) on popular open models (opt-6b-class).
- Cost: 20% lower per-token cost for standard chat workloads for customers adopting Optimize recommendations.
- Adoption: 150+ customers migrated to v2 pricing or Dedicated tiers within 90 days of launch.

Product Requirements (PRD)

1) Functional requirements

- FR-001: Single API endpoints for: /v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank. Backwards compatible with v1 semantics; new optional params must be additive.
- FR-002: Model catalog exposes model variant metadata: architecture, fp/quantization, memory footprint, preferred hardware, and latency/cost profile.
- FR-003: Streaming responses support chunked tokens + delta compression for low-bandwidth clients.
- FR-004: Tool/function calling remains supported; payload size limits and schema validation must be enforced.
- FR-005: Per-route rollout policies: canary %, A/B, automatic fallback to compatible model variant when SLO/health degrades.

2) Non-functional requirements (NFRs)

- NFR-001 (Availability): Hosted API 99.95% uptime. Dedicated SLA options: 99.9% / 99.95% depending on contract.
- NFR-002 (Latency): Target p95 < 300ms for short context (<128 tokens) on standard models; p95 < 600ms for 512-token flows.
- NFR-003 (Cost transparency): token-level cost breakdowns in Console within 15 minutes of usage.
- NFR-004 (Security): All customer data encrypted in-flight and at-rest; KMS integration for Private deployments.
- NFR-005 (Scalability): System supports 2x baseline traffic for top 100 customers without degradation.

Requirements table (condensed)

| ID | Type | Description | Owner |
|-----|------|-------------|-------|
| FR-001 | Functional | Unified API endpoints | Product / API |
| FR-002 | Functional | Model catalog metadata | Model Onboarding |
| NFR-001 | Non-functional | 99.95% hosted availability | SRE / Platform |
| NFR-003 | Non-functional | Token-level cost reporting (15m) | Console / Billing |

Design: high-level architecture and decisions

Scope: Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem packaging).

Key design principles

- Single control plane, pluggable runtime: customers use the same API and rollout config; runtime selection and kernel targeting is handled by the serving layer.
- Cost-aware routing: route by latency/cost/region/customer-tier with automatic fallback.
- Observe-first: include tracing hooks, per-route SLO dashboards, and automated regression detection tied to evaluation prompt sets.

Architecture overview (summary)

- Ingress layer: Edge proxies handle authentication (API key/OAuth), rate limits, and request validation.
- Router & Policy Engine: routes requests according to model compatibility rules, customer routing policies (latency vs cost), and real-time health data.
- Serving Runtime Pools: GPU-optimized inference engines grouped by model family and quantization profile. Pools support continuous batching and KV cache sharing.
- Telemetry & Metrics pipeline: per-token cost, latency histograms, request traces, and evaluation hooks forwarded to Console.

Design Decisions and Trade-offs

- Kernel selection at runtime vs ahead-of-time compilation: choose runtime selection for rapid model onboarding and fallback flexibility; compile common kernels for top-10 models to optimize hot paths.
- Prefix/KV caching consistency model: use conservative TTL-based invalidation to avoid staleness at the cost of slightly reduced caching hit rates for rarely-updated policies.

Component Ownership and Interfaces

- API layer: eng-developer-experience (owner: Jordan Kim) - endpoint semantics, SDKs, and docs.
- Router & Policy Engine: eng-platform (owner: Priya Kapoor) - rollout policies, routing rules.
- Serving Runtime: eng-serving-runtime (owner: Marco Ruiz) - kernel selection, batching, quantization.
- Console & Billing UI: eng-platform + finance (owner: Liam Chen) - cost reporting, pricing UI.

Implementation notes and examples

- Example API call (generation):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY"
  -d '{"model":"redwood-opt-6b-q4f16", "input":"Summarize the meeting:", "max_tokens":128, "stream":true }'

- Recommended runtime config snippet (YAML):

runtime_pool:
  name: opt-6b-q4f16
  gpu_type: a100-80gb
  quantization: q4f16
  batch_window_ms: 12
  prefetch_kv_cache: true

Roadmap & Themes (Q3 - Q4 2026)

Themes by quarter:

- Q3 2026: "Consistency & Cost" - unify APIs, release Optimize v2 recommendations, launch pricing v2 beta, kernel optimizations for opt-6b class.
- Q4 2026: "Enterprise Readiness" - Dedicated SLA improvements, Private release automation (on-prem packaging), audit & compliance evidence flow.
- Q1 2027: "Scale & Ops" - autoscaling improvements for Dedicated, multi-region active-active routing, longer-term retention for observability.

Planned milestones (quarter-level)

1. 2026-07-01: API contract freeze and SDK updates started.
2. 2026-08-15: Pricing & Packaging v2 public launch (console + docs).
3. 2026-09-15: Hosted API rollout with model-catalog metadata and per-route rollouts (canary support).
4. 2026-10-10: Dedicated tier pricing published and Reserved Capacity contract templates updated.
5. 2026-11-30: Private deployment automation (first GA pilot customers).

Pricing & Packaging notes (v2)

Principles:
- Transparent per-unit pricing with optional committed discounts for Dedicated.
- Align incentives: recommendations in Redwood Optimize should reduce customer unit-cost and are opt-in.
- Simpler tiers: Developer (self-serve), Team (growth), Enterprise (sales-assisted).

High-level tariffs (indicative)

| Tier | Hosted | Dedicated | Key features |
|------|--------|-----------|--------------|
| Developer | $0.0009 / token-gen (short) | N/A | Free sandbox, 60k tokens/month free-tier, community support |
| Team | $0.0006 / token-gen (short) | $X/month reserved | SLA: 99.9%, dedicated console views, 90-day billing |
| Enterprise | Custom | Custom (SLA 99.95%) | On-prem options, KMS/HSM integration, enterprise support |

Notes:
- Final unit prices vary by model class (opt-6b-class vs opt-30b-class) and quantization profile. Console will show a model-specific per-token rate before request submission.
- Dedicated reserved capacity uses monthly commits with overage priced at on-demand rates.

Release Notes (Q3 2026 public launch - 2026-08-15)

Highlights:
- Unified API endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank (backwards compatible).
- Model catalog: model metadata and per-model latency/cost estimates in Console.
- Per-route rollouts: canary and automatic fallback to compatible model variants.
- Pricing v2: Developer and Team plans published; Enterprise sales playbook updated.
- Optimize recommendations: batch size, quantization, and caching suggestions in Console.

Breaking changes and migration guidance

- No breaking contract changes for core endpoints; SDKs have largely additive changes. Customers using custom integrations that parse raw runtime headers should validate against new header keys (X-Redwood-Model-Variant, X-Redwood-Route-Policy).
- Billing: customers on legacy pricing will be contacted and offered a migration path with a 60-day opt-in window for pricing v2. Finance will run manual reconciliations for early adopters.

Rollout & Launch Plan

1) Pre-launch (2026-07-01 -> 2026-08-01)
   - API contract freeze and SDK beta releases. Owners: API (Jordan Kim), SDK (Alex Gomez).
   - Internal dogfooding: platform team to migrate three internal product stacks to the unified endpoints.
   - Sales enablement: pricing playbook, updated pitch decks, and closed-won migration paths.

2) Canary launch (2026-08-01 -> 2026-08-10)
   - Canary route for 5% of new traffic; monitor SLOs (latency, error rate) and feature flags.
   - Run load against serving pools with synthetic traffic to validate autoscaling and batching behavior.

3) Gradual rollout (2026-08-10 -> 2026-08-15)
   - Move to 25% -> 50% -> 100% over three steady-state checkpoints (24h each) if SLOs met.
   - Post-launch 72-hour intensive monitoring window; incident response team on-call (Owner: eng-sre).

4) Post-launch (from 2026-08-15)
   - Evaluate KPIs at 7/30/90-day intervals: adoption, cost savings, error budgets, customer feedback.
   - Feature flags to enable/disable Optimize recommendations per-customer.

Monitoring, SLOs and Alerts

- SLOs:
  - Availability: 99.95% (hosted API) - alert on 30m rolling error budget burn >50%.
  - Latency: p95 < 300ms for <128 token flows - alert if p95 exceeds target for two consecutive 15m windows.
  - Error rate: request error rate <1% across production namespace - alert at 0.5% sustained over 10m.

- Dashboards: per-route latency heatmap, per-model cost hourly breakdown, top error sources.
- Runbooks: see runbooks in eng-sre/runbooks (links below) for escalation steps.

Open risks & Mitigations

- Risk: Failing to achieve latency targets on cheaper quantized variants. Mitigation: maintain fallback to fp16 variants and pre-compile top kernels; rollout quantization recommendations as opt-in.
- Risk: Customer confusion on pricing changes. Mitigation: phased communications, webinar with finance/sales, migration credits for early adopters.
- Risk: On-prem packaging complexity for Private. Mitigation: dedicated engineering sprint for install automation and hardened test harness.

2. Switch integration to /v1/generate or /v1/chat with no-op flags.

4. Enable Optimize recommendations in Console for cost savings (opt-in) and validate output quality with your eval prompt sets.
